posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

Observing the early universe would be such a fascinating and relaxing experience... or would it be?

We imagine advanced alien civilizations building gigantic spaceships, Dyson spheres and empires spanning entire galaxies. But what if true technological progress goes in exactly the opposite direction? Not outward into space, but deeper and deeper into the smallest layers of reality?

What is the Barrow Scale? How powerful could a civilization become by mastering DNA, and even fundamental particles, and could the universe already be filled with godlike civilizations hiding in plain sight? Watch
Let's visit some of the most dangerous neighbourhoods... in space!

Our curiosity to learn more about the stars is endless. Today, some scientists pursue their passion by building large telescopes that are able to capture the faintest glimmer of stars billions of light-years away. Some telescopes are even launched from Earth to get a clearer view outside the atmosphere. But what about the opportunity to see the stars with your own eyes, unfiltered? Astronauts, like the one that can be seen on the September page of our 12,026 Human Era calendar, say nothing compa

Could humans evolve to be able to fly some day? Flying like a bird would require way more than just wings. Hollow bones, giant chest muscles, rewired nerves, and absurd amounts of food might allow you to fly, but all of this would transform you into something barely human anymore.

In a battle against cancer, could viruses be our allies? When Croatian virologist Dr. Beata Halassy’s breast cancer returned for the third time, she made a bold decision: to experiment on herself using millions of viruses grown in her own lab. Viruses love cancer cells, which helped her turn them into a weapon against her own tumor.

What happens when you infect cancer with a virus, and could virotherapy become a powerful new tool against cancer? Watch our full video to find out!

What if continents and oceans switched places? The Pacific becomes a supercontinent. Earth's deepest point is Everest Deep, and is almost nine kilometers below sea-level. And the Mid-Atlantic Canyon divides the world from pole to pole. Life finds a way but struggles in this new, upside-down world. This all sounds cool, until the oxygen runs out.

Pigeons are basically GPS Drones with superpowers. They can pinpoint their own location hundreds of kilometers from their roosts and navigate home autonomously, only using smell, the Sun, and even Earth’s magnetic field.

No one works harder than our rover driver Yolk, who is tirelessly collecting nuggets every day so that the space station can function smoothly.

Have you already started your space adventure? Star Birds, which we developed together with our friends at @toukana_interactive, is available on Steam!
Two billion years ago, the world’s first nuclear reactors appeared in Oklo, Gabon. They were NOT made by humans and were self-regulating and accident-free.

In the late 9th century, Vikings have raided kingdom after kingdom and nearly conquered all of England. Wealthy monasteries and defenseless nuns were especially tempting targets and often suffered great losses. However, all of that stopped when Vikings were confronted by princess Aethelflaed, daughter of Alfred the Great.

Who was Lady of Mercia, and how did she shape the history of England by becoming Vikings' greatest nightmare? Watch our latest Nightshift video to find out! 🌚

recentPosts.caption:
Photographer @okirakuoki captures cats in their funniest poses. 🐈⁠
⁠
From awkward stretches to completely unexpected expressions, his photos show just how funny cats can be when they’re simply being themselves.⁠
⁠
And the last photo might just be the best one. 😂

@travel_earth_fr takes us on a completely different way to experience Mont-Saint-Michel. 🌊🇫🇷⁠
⁠
Walking across the bay to Tombelaine Rock means going barefoot through the sand, crossing tidal rivers, and even learning how quicksand forms and how to safely get out of it. ⁠
⁠
The quicksand here forms when water saturates the sand, making it temporarily lose its structure under pressure and behave more like a liquid.⁠
⁠
The experience covers around 7 km in about 3 hours, with the route and condi

In Aymara, the Indigenous language of Bolivia’s Altiplano, “Samkani” means “the one who dreams.”⁠
⁠
That’s exactly what this new camp promises to deliver.⁠
⁠
Samkani Camp will sit in the middle of Bolivia’s Salar de Uyuni, the world’s largest salt flat, with just five private Airstream suites surrounded by one of the most surreal places on Earth.⁠
⁠
Guests will have private dining, space to relax under the stars, and the chance to explore the salt flats from their own secluded base.⁠
⁠
The camp

One of Costa Rica’s most spectacular bird sightings. 🌿👑⁠
⁠
The Tropical Royal Flycatcher may look fairly ordinary for most of the year, but during nesting season, it reveals an incredible colorful crest that’s usually kept hidden.⁠
⁠
The nesting season runs from March to May, making it an especially exciting time to spot this beautiful species in Costa Rica.⁠
⁠
Would you be lucky enough to catch this moment?⁠
🎥: @josepabpm

The roof of this café was designed to let a tree grow through. 🌳⁠
⁠
Harudot Chonburi in Thailand was designed by @idinarchitects around a baobab tree that was already growing on the site. The architects opened the roof and created space for the tree to continue growing through the café.⁠
⁠
The name Harudot comes from “Haru,” Japanese for spring and new beginnings, and “dot,” representing a starting point.⁠
⁠
Photos by: @dofskyground

Seven travel creator opportunities worth looking at right now:

- Beautiful Destinations Academy in Dubai. 12 weeks of training in cinematography, editing and production, run with Dubai’s tourism department. Applications open now.

- Virgin’s Head of Yes. £75,000 in the UK or $100,000 in the US for six months. You apply by posting a video with #HeadOfYes. No following needed. Closes 20 October.

- New Mexico True seasonal campaigns. Hosted trips throug

This is what a tiny meerkat looks like. ⁠
⁠
This little meerkat was only about as tall as a thumb, but somehow gave the photographers one of their most unforgettable moments in the bush.⁠
⁠
Captured at Kamfersboom Borehole in the Kgalagadi Transfrontier Park, South Africa.⁠
⁠
By: @a.z__photography_

This is Icelandic weather in one video. 😂💨⁠
@renmoldovantravel captured the moment strong winds were blowing the waterfall back uphill, because apparently, even the water isn’t safe from Iceland’s weather.⁠
A perfect reminder that in Iceland, you can experience four seasons, wild winds, and a little bit of chaos all in the same day.⁠
⁠
Have you experienced Icelandic weather yet?⁠
🎥: @renmoldovantravel

This church is covered in gray and white stripes. 🖤⁠
⁠
The Church of San Giovanni Battista in Mogno, Switzerland, was designed by architect Mario Botta and built between 1994 and 1996.⁠
⁠
The church replaced an older building that was destroyed by an avalanche in 1986. Botta used alternating layers of marble and gneiss to create its distinctive striped pattern, with the stone coming from nearby quarries in the region.⁠
⁠
By: @lerichti

A dress that carries a story of healing. ⁠
Taiwan, where Jingle Dress dancers were invited to share this meaningful Indigenous tradition at Fo Guang Shan.⁠
⁠
The Jingle Dress is decorated with rows of metal cones whose sounds echo the rhythm of falling rain. 🌧️ The jingles are traditionally associated with healing, with water symbolizing the washing away of pain, grief, trauma, and illness.⁠
⁠
A powerful tradition to witness. 🩵⁠
🎥: @aeriusbentonbanai

This ancient town was built around a waterfall. ⁠
⁠
Furong Town in Hunan, China, is famous for the 60-meter waterfall that flows right through the town before dropping into the valley below.⁠
⁠
Wooden houses, narrow paths, and old buildings line the cliffs around the falls, creating one of the most unusual townscapes in China.⁠
⁠
About 22,000 permanent residents live in Furong Town, primarily consisting of the Tujia ethnic minority alongside Han Chinese residents.⁠
⁠
By: @allen.fu88⁠

A Highland cow with quite the impressive stretch. 🐮😂⁠
This fluffy guy reaching out with those long horns, a pretty fun close-up of one of Scotland’s most recognizable animals.⁠
⁠
Have you ever seen a Highland cow in person?⁠
🎥: @passportunities

Since then, conservationists have worked with local landowners to reduce threats to this rare species and preserve its habitat. While they continue to secure land for the largest species, organizations across Africa—like Kenya's Pangolin Project and the Tikki Hywood Foundation in Cameroon and Zimbabwe—are working to protect pangolins from black-market trade.

In this species, the males carry bright pink eggs, carefully attached to a brood patch under their tails. Endemic to Australian waters, these extraordinary creatures are uniquely adapted to their marine environment. Their delicate, leaflike appendages allow them to effortlessly blend into the seaweed and kelp they call home.
